reviews.text: I've been taking care of my cat since she was zero years old. They detected the possibility of struvite crystals early on, and I've been careful about her food ever since. They always listen carefully to my concerns during other procedures, and I feel comfortable consulting with both the doctor and the nurses.

It took me a while to process my feelings, and I even hesitated about whether to leave a review.

Rather than a complaint to the hospital, I'm deliberately leaving this as a record so that other pet owners and dogs don't have to go through the same thing.

My dog's gums around his back teeth were slightly swollen, so I took him to this hospital on a day when my regular vet was closed.

The X-ray results indicated "gingivitis with pus accumulation," and I was told that "it will heal if the tooth is extracted and the pus is drained."

Because my dog ​​was elderly and had weak kidneys, the extraction procedure requiring general anesthesia was deemed difficult, and I was prescribed antibiotics with the suggestion to "wait for the pus to drain naturally."

The explanation was thorough, but I believed it, and my decision was delayed.

Although he was 16 years old and had some tartar buildup, all of his teeth were still intact.

Afterward, the swelling rapidly worsened, and I became suspicious, so I took him back to my regular vet, where he was diagnosed with "malignant melanoma (oral cancer)."

Despite our best efforts in treatment, we couldn't stop the progression of the disease, and he passed away three weeks after the diagnosis.

This all happened in less than a month after we first visited this clinic.

While I acknowledge my own lack of knowledge, I still question why a pathology test wasn't suggested at the initial consultation, and why the diagnosis ended with just gingivitis.

I deeply regret that they didn't at least mention the possibility of cancer.

Later, I received a letter (a promotional postcard) asking, "How is he doing now?", which broke my heart.

I sincerely hope this experience will be helpful to other pet owners and their dogs.

I've taken my dog ​​there for checkups several times, but it's always "tests, tests, tests"...

All my dog-owning friends in the neighborhood say the same thing.

Of course, I understand that there are times when tests and diagnoses must be made immediately due to urgency, but other clinics consider all possibilities and patterns before testing, prioritizing and eliminating options to make a diagnosis. They are considerate of the owner's feelings and try to minimize the burden on the owner. I felt that this clinic lacked that kind of empathetic approach.

My dog-owning friends all share the same opinion. Instead of just relocating and expanding the hospital, I wish they had a doctor who would examine patients from a different perspective, rather than relying solely on test results. I would like to go back there if they did.

Thank you for your help.

Thanks to you, Momo 🍑 is feeling a little better. …

My cat was unwell, so I sought a second opinion at this clinic.

The doctor was a woman, but she diagnosed my cat with "possibly FIP" without performing the necessary blood tests required to suspect FIP.

FIP is a disease that requires immediate attention, so please go to a hospital that specializes in FIP.

I'm writing this review because only the owner can protect their beloved cat.
Thank you for your continued support.

I had my pet examined around noon today. It was a last-minute appointment, but thank you so much for your kind and thorough care until the very end. I tried calling, but the signal was bad and the call was cut off, so I'm writing this review instead. Thank you so much.
I was relieved to find out that they also treat small animals.

We used their pet hotel service for small animals.

They kindly allowed us to bring anything we wanted to recreate their usual home environment, which we greatly appreciated.

At home, we scatter treats in the cage at night for a treasure hunt, and it seems the nurses took good care of that during our stay.

Upon pickup, they gave us a progress chart detailing daily meals, bowel movements, and overall condition. I was amazed at the level of care they put into small animals! Seeing how carefully they cared for our pet gave us great peace of mind.

Some time later, we received a postcard with a photo of our pet taken during their stay! Even though they care for so many animals in the outpatient and inpatient departments, it was clear they cared for our pet with genuine love and care. I assume the nurses primarily handled the hotel care; thank you so much.

During the trial stay, they performed an ultrasound, and the doctor's explanation was very thorough. They also took the time to discuss our concerns about our pet's senior years.

We have since moved, so we won't be visiting again, but I can confidently recommend this hospital to anyone in the neighborhood.

I've been using your services every month for the past two years. Thank you for always explaining everything so carefully. My dog ​​isn't scared at all and seems happy to come. I look forward to continuing to use your services in the future.

My two cats are patients here. During their regular checkup this year, one of my cats was found to have a liver abnormality, so they are now going to the clinic once a month. The doctor is kind and explains everything carefully.
It's clean, has a warm atmosphere, and the examinations are thorough, so I feel comfortable coming here.
